messages.author: 1a09129d38549286
messages.subject: Repository or Plot Builder templates?
parts:
Hi,

The templates of Deducer's Plot Builder are a wonderful time-saver in
graphics production, and I think that users would benefit a lot from
having a place to share and look for contributed templates, apart from
the ones available in the Deducer package.

For instance, some of my colleagues regret that the pie chart has been
removed from the set of standard templates in Deducer 0.6.x. I know
that pie charts are not considered good practice by the "R
establishment", so I won't ask for its being restored. But the fact is
that many people use them, and our clients often expect (and sometimes
claim) that kind of representation in reports, so it's convenient to
have that template available somewhere, instead of having to combine
the non-standard plot of stacked bars with polar coordinates every
time someone wants to create such a graphic.

And that's only an example of useful (or not-so-useful) templates that
could be shared by users, complementing and enlarging the "standard"
set of Deducer.

Now, I wonder if there is a recommended place to share them. I'm aware
that there is a section in the help page of the Plot Builder (http://
www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.PlotBuilder) with "Additional
templates", but I don't know if Ian expects it to be some kind of
public repository, or it would be better to use some other place.

Regards,
Helios

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Repository or Plot Builder templates?
parts:
The reason I remove the pie chart template was mainly because I found
it sub-optimal from a GUI design point of view. I felt that it would
be better if it was implemented as a custom dialog. That said, I don't
see myself having the time to actually implement it any time in the
near future.

I think the open repository is a good idea, and am open to suggestions
regarding where/how to host it.

Best,
Ian
